254zhoutiangong.excerpt: The microcosmic orbit practice makes true qi circulate through the body along the orbit, thereby moving qi and activating blood, dispersing stagnation and dissolving stasis, and restoring essence to nourish the brain — achieving resistance to disease and immunity, health and longevity.

255haorenge.title: The Song of a Good Man (Annotated)
255haorenge.author: Lü Xinwu
255haorenge.excerpt: Original note: His name was Kun, courtesy name Shujian, a native of Ningling, a jinshi of the Jiajing era of the Ming dynasty, who rose to the post of Junior Minister of Justice (vice-minister of the Ministry of Justice).

256chengxinxingshan.title: Doing Good with a Sincere Heart
256chengxinxingshan.excerpt: Translation: The coming of calamity and fortune has no other cause; all are summoned by one's own thoughts and actions. The retribution for good and evil in thought and deed follows like a shadow following its form — doing evil brings calamity, doing good brings fortune.

257nizhuanshuailao.title: Reversing Aging Through the Practice of the Jiaji Point
257nizhuanshuailao.author: Zhang Xingchun
257nizhuanshuailao.excerpt: Constantly hold this mind, withdrawing it to conceal it in the jiaji point, and guard it without leaving.

258quanzhenqizizhuan.title: Biographies of the Seven Disciples of Quanzhen
258quanzhenqizizhuan.excerpt: In this world there is nothing truly difficult, only those whose hearts are set on it.

259jingzongrumen.title: An Introduction to the Pure Land School
259jingzongrumen.author: Zhanran
259jingzongrumen.excerpt: The purpose of studying Buddhism is to become a Buddha and deliver living beings. For ordinary people to cultivate and realize Buddhahood, there are two great stages: first, transcending the cycle of rebirth; second, perfectly realizing the Buddha-fruit. The goal of the Buddhist practitioner in this life is to transcend the six realms of rebirth.

260jinianjiguan.title: Observing the Mind in Buddha-Recitation
260jinianjiguan.author: Zhanran
260jinianjiguan.excerpt: Observing the mind in Buddha-recitation means that while reciting, one observes the present thought (reciting and observing at once). This is an exceedingly incisive and wondrous method that can steadily achieve: the moment the Buddha's name is raised, deluded thoughts entirely vanish.

261lengqiejing.title: The Lankavatara Sutra
261lengqiejing.excerpt: Composed by Jiang Zhiqi, Grand Master for Court Discussion, Direct Scholar of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, Commissioner for Salt and Alum Regulation and Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Jianghuai, Jing, and Zhe Circuits, Senior Guardian, and recipient of the Purple and Gold Fish Pouch.

269yigenianforendezishu.title: The Dual Cultivation of Nature and Life

269yigenianforendezishu.excerpt: [Dual cultivation of nature and life] Cultivating nature: liberation of self-nature (transcending the six realms of rebirth); cultivating life: health and longevity.

272nianfojingju.title: Maxims on Buddha-Recitation (Four Items)
272nianfojingju.author: Venerable Huxi
272nianfojingju.excerpt: All who practice the Pure Land must clearly aim to defeat birth and death, not merely talk and let it go. One should reflect that impermanence is swift and time waits for no one; one must treat this as the one thing to do. If one advances and retreats by halves, half believing and half doubting, what will that accomplish when the end comes? How can one transcend the cycle of rebirth?

273wumingmeng.title: The Dream of Ignorance

273wumingmeng.excerpt: Question: Why is it said that “all dharmas are illusions”?

274baizhangyehu.title: Baizhang's Wild Fox
274baizhangyehu.author: Annotated by Zhiyu
274baizhangyehu.excerpt: Whenever the master (Chan Master Baizhang) ascended the hall, an old man followed the assembly to hear the Dharma. One day, after the assembly had dispersed, only the old man remained. The master asked: “Who are you?” The old man said: “I am not a human being. In the time of Kasyapa Buddha I once lived on this mountain. A student asked me: ‘Does a great practitioner still fall into cause and effect or not?’...”

275zhengdaogezhu.title: Annotated Song of Enlightenment
275zhengdaogezhu.author: Annotated by Zhanran
275zhengdaogezhu.excerpt: The Song of Enlightenment is the state of awakening from the dream of ignorance. For example, the song says: “When the dharmakaya awakens, there is not a single thing,” and “In the dream there are clearly the six realms; after awakening there is nothing, not even the great chiliocosm.” Like the Diamond Sutra, the Heart Sutra, and the Platform Sutra, its core is the realization of the patience of the unborn...

278-1jianxingshixing.title: Perceiving the Nature: It Is the Mind
278-1jianxingshixing.author: Annotated by Mingde
278-1jianxingshixing.excerpt: [Ananda, answer me first: you saw the radiant fist. What causes this fist to be radiant? How does it become a fist? With what do you see it? Ananda said: The Buddha's whole body is born of the gold of the Jambu river, brilliant as a jewel mountain, born of purity, hence its radiance. In truth, my eyes see the five fingers, curled and clenched, shown to people, hence the form of a fist.]

278-2jianxingbudong.title: Perceiving the Nature: It Is Unmoving
278-2jianxingbudong.author: Annotated by Mingde
278-2jianxingbudong.excerpt: [At that time the World-Honored One extended his radiant hand, with its web-like marks of the Tushita cotton, opened his five fingers, and admonished Ananda and the assembly: “When I first attained the Way, in the Deer Park I said to the five bhikshus such as Ajnata-kaundinya and to your fourfold assembly: All living beings fail to attain bodhi and arhatship because they are misled by the defilements of adventitious dust. What did you awaken to at that time, that you now...”]

278-3jianxingbumie.excerpt: [At that time King Prasenajit rose and addressed the Buddha: “In the past, before I had received the Buddha's admonitions, I met Kaccayana and Vairatiputra, who both said this body is annihilated after death and called that nirvana. Though I have now met the Buddha, I still harbor doubts. How can one demonstrate and know this mind's state of non-arising and non-ceasing? Now in this assembly, those with outflows...”]

280kuoranwusheng.title: Vast Emptiness, No Sage
280kuoranwusheng.author: Zhiyu
280kuoranwusheng.excerpt: [Emperor Wu of Liang asked Master Bodhidharma: “What is the first principle of the holy truth?” Bodhidharma said: “Vast emptiness, no sage!” The emperor said: “Who then is facing me?” Bodhidharma said: “I do not know.” The emperor did not understand, and Bodhidharma crossed the river to Wei.]

281yinianbusheng.title: Not a Single Thought Arises, Yet All Is Clear
281yinianbusheng.author: Zhanran
281yinianbusheng.excerpt: Question: Is “not a single thought arises, yet all is clear” a good state or a bad state? Why do some Chan masters severely scold this state?

282qishianxin.title: Begging the Master to Pacify the Mind
282qishianxin.author: Annotated by Zhiyu
282qishianxin.excerpt: [On the night of the ninth day of the twelfth month of that year, it snowed heavily. Huike stood firm and unmoving, and by dawn the snow had piled past his knees. The patriarch, moved to pity, asked: “You have stood long in the snow; what do you seek?” Huike wept: “I only beg the master, in his compassion, to open the gate of sweet dew and widely deliver all beings.” The patriarch said: “The unsurpassed wondrous Way of the Buddhas requires striving through long kalpas, doing what is hard to do...”]

283kongjudeyuantou.excerpt: By Eckhart Tolle; translated by Zhang Defen.

284erzhonggenben.title: The Two Roots
284erzhonggenben.author: Annotated by Zhiyu
284erzhonggenben.excerpt: [All living beings, since time without beginning, continue in birth and death because they do not know the permanent true mind, the pure, luminous essence of nature, and use instead deluded thoughts; because these thoughts are not true, there is the cycle of transmigration.]

285jingzhongjie.title: Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's Verse Admonishing the Assembly
285jingzhongjie.excerpt: Time flies swiftly, and human life is impermanent. Buddhist practitioners must be vigilant at all times; never be careless, frolic and play, and waste time, only to regret it endlessly.

290zixingsanyi.author: Zhanran
290zixingsanyi.excerpt: Question: Many sutras and treatises say all dharmas lack self-nature. Why then does the Lankavatara Sutra say “just as an ox lacks horse-nature and a horse lacks ox-nature, it is not that they lack self-nature”?

291xiuxingdezhendi.title: The True Meaning of Practice
291xiuxingdezhendi.excerpt: The mind is like a continuous river. If you cannot use your practice to seize hold of each present moment, then your mantra recitation, visualization, chanting, meditation, and even the lofty view you profess and the lofty conduct you display are all a waste of time.

292wuzhongzuiqiangdadeliliang.title: The Five Most Powerful Forces
292wuzhongzuiqiangdadeliliang.author: The True Meaning of Practice
292wuzhongzuiqiangdadeliliang.excerpt: For practice to become a way of life, one should cultivate the five forces. If we possess the five forces, bodhicitta will naturally arise in the mind.

293jgj-zhu.title: Annotated Diamond Sutra
293jgj-zhu.author: Annotated by Zhanran

302xinj.title: An Elucidation of the Heart Sutra
302xinj.author: An Elucidation of the Heart Sutra
302xinj.excerpt: The Buddha preached the Dharma for forty-nine years, twenty-two of which were devoted to the Prajñā scriptures. One may say the Prajñā scriptures are the soul of the entire Buddhadharma, the Diamond Sutra is the essence of the Prajñā scriptures, and the Heart Sutra is the essence of the Diamond Sutra. Hence for a thousand years the Heart Sutra has been known in every household and loved by all...

303liuzutanjing.title: An Elucidation of the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch
303liuzutanjing.author: Annotated by Zhanran
303liuzutanjing.excerpt: The Platform Sutra is the only work of indigenous Chinese Buddhism honored with the title “sutra.” It gives a systematic and comprehensive exposition of the theory and practice of the sudden teaching of “perceiving one's original nature and becoming a Buddha by seeing the nature,” and its appearance marks the formal establishment of Chinese Chan, radiant with glory.

304fozangj.title: Selected Passages from the Buddha Repository Sutra, Annotated
304fozangj.author: Selected and annotated by Zhanran
304fozangj.excerpt: The Buddha Repository Sutra, in three fascicles, was translated by Master Kumārajīva on the twelfth day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Hongshi (405) in the Later Qin. The sutra has ten chapters, discussing the true mark of all dharmas as unborn and unceasing, markless and unconditioned. 402nianfolun.author: Compiled and annotated by Zhanran
402nianfolun.excerpt: With one utterance of the Buddha's name, unmixed with other concerns, ten recitations achieve the work and instantly transcend many kalpas.

403chanjing.title: The Essential Principles of Chan and Pure Land (Annotated Instructions of Master Hanshan)
403chanjing.author: Compiled and annotated by Zhanran
403chanjing.excerpt: Looking over Master Hanshan's entire life, like Master Yongming (the sixth Pure Land patriarch) and Master Chewu (the twelfth), he was outstanding in both the cultivation and propagation of Chan and Pure Land, and he is listed in the Records of Pure Land Sages. So he is a patriarch of both the Chan school and the Pure Land school...

It is the original draft of Master Liaoyu, published after revision by Master Yinguang, so it also embodies Master Yinguang's own experience and insight in cultivating the samadhi of Buddha-recitation — a rare and precious document of the Buddha-recitation method. 502yuanjuejingjj.title: An Elucidation of the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment
502yuanjuejingjj.author: Annotated by Zhanran
502yuanjuejingjj.excerpt: The full title of the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment is “The Great and Vast Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment,” in twelve chapters. In it Shakyamuni Buddha, through dialogues with twelve great bodhisattvas, expounds the wondrous principle of the Tathagata's perfect enlightenment (the perfectly awakened self-nature) and the methods of practice.
